A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoGUI pipeline and dataset. Their main text, tables, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original human annotation comparisons, rejection and verification ablations, VLM fine-tuning experiments, scaling results, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original annotation-quality and grounding experiments and adds Qwen2-VL fine-tuning results and AITW agent-planning experiments.

M1.justification: The annotation, rejection, and two-verifier pipeline remains intact. V2 changes the stated coordinate representation from [0, 99] to [0, 999] and adds a downstream inference adaptation: a proprietary planner describes expected functionality, and a fine-tuned grounding model supplies target coordinates (Section 5 and Appendix C).

E1.justification: V2 adds AITW action-planning evaluation across five categories and removes RefExp evaluation. ScreenSpot-v2 supplements the retained multi-platform grounding coverage. Section 3.1 also newly reports including AndroidControl and MobileViews trajectories, although their contributions to the unchanged dataset totals are not quantified.

E2.justification: Table 4 removes the three LLaVA configurations and adds GPT-4o, Llama-3.2-Vision-Instruct, UGround-v1-7B, and OS-ATLAS. Table 6 introduces proprietary-planner comparisons with and without the AutoGUI-trained grounder. The earlier mixed AutoGUI/SeeClick-data experiment corresponds to the renamed SeeClick w/ AutoGUI row. Table 5 retains the same two alternative annotation types despite v2's inconsistent caption count.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen2-VL-7B fine-tuning and an AITW evaluation protocol using step accuracy and click accuracy. It revises the stated coordinate normalization to [0, 999] and presents scaling through accuracy averaged across benchmarks. The existing 25k/125k/702k training scales and one-epoch, eight-A100 setup remain.

E4.justification: V2 extends data-size sensitivity testing to Qwen2-VL, replaces RefExp with MoTIF in the annotation-type ablation, and reports a train/test element-overlap check in Appendix A.1. The rejection/verification ablations and appendix failure cases and distance histograms are retained. Detailed rejection-consistency evidence is omitted.

E5.justification: V1 specifies three-run consistency tests using 100 valid samples and 46 invalid samples. V2 retains the 94.5% consistency claim but omits that experiment's run setup and explanation of consistency; these details do not reappear in its appendix. The separate three-run statement for Table 3 remains. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds and removes many results and revises retained entries: Qwen2-VL's ScreenSpot score changes from 26.1 to 66.4, and Qwen-VL-AutoGUI702k's FuncPred score changes from 43.1 to 48.7. V2 adds Qwen2-VL fine-tuning, ScreenSpot-v2, and AITW results while removing RefExp and detailed smaller-scale benchmark rows. The 79.3% rejection-consistency result disappears. These reported revisions do not establish controlled performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: The annotation, rejection, and verification expressions and the correctness and grounding-accuracy definitions retain their mathematical substance. Displayed equations become inline expressions. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs; the new agent metrics concern evaluation protocol.

C1.justification: The central claims about scalable automatic functionality annotation, human-comparable annotation correctness, and improved grounding remain. V2 adds an abstract and introduction claim about assisting GUI agents through grounding refinement and softens the assertion that previous datasets never provided such annotations to saying they hardly provide them.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the AITW results as correcting proprietary planners' coordinate-localization errors and explicitly limits the experiment to demonstrating potential use rather than establishing superiority over specialized agents. The earlier limitations concerning mobile coverage, task-oriented trajectories, and read-only interactions are retained and moved into the main text.

D1.justification: V2 adds source licenses, Qwen-VL LoRA rank and alpha, Qwen2-VL hyperparameters, training times, framework names, and downstream action-routing details. It removes the task-template table, tokenizer explanation, explicit trajectory-based split-construction description, and VWB instruction-rewriting disclosure. These change reproducibility documentation without establishing corresponding implementation changes in every case.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and Table 1 substantially refocus positioning toward recent GUI grounding datasets and agents, including UGround, OS-ATLAS, ShowUI, and Aguvis, and distinguish new contextual annotations from dataset aggregation. Earlier web-navigation coverage is removed, and verification-related citations expand. Publication updates to retained works such as CogAgent and Ferret-UI are not new research additions.

P1.justification: V2 extensively condenses and rewrites the introduction, related work, method explanations, and results narrative. Data-quality analysis moves into Section 3.6, dataset exploration is consolidated, limitations move into the main text, and a dedicated application section and corresponding appendix section are introduced.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and extensively reorganizes displays. It removes the airport illustration, redraws the annotation-comparison figure, restructures Tables 1 and 4, and adds a scaling plot, agent diagram/results table, license table, hyperparameter table, and benchmark examples. The human-checking criteria move to the appendix; existing appendix case figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens experimental relevance by testing AutoGUI fine-tuning on the already capable Qwen2-VL and comparing against newer GUI specialists, extending v1's evidence from Qwen-VL and SliME. Added licenses, LoRA settings, and training times improve reproducibility. These benefits are moderated by lost uncertainty and protocol details and unclear AITW aggregation: Table 6 reports 18.37 for a row whose displayed category scores average 20.60, without explaining weighting. The net improvement is therefore limited.
